anchors.claimScope: The Design route produces a reviewable handoff bundle from a bounded brief, selected direction, prototype evidence, and explicit implementation limits; it does not claim production completion.
anchors.principleStatement: Design ends with a handoff bundle whose source, intent, states, responsive and accessibility rules, evidence, scope, and unresolved assumptions are explicit; implementation and production verification remain separate continuations.
changeTriggers: The approved Design route, stop condition, or handoff evidence contract changes

observations: Issue #13 defines Design as a route with its own entry, evidence, stop, and optional Engineering continuation.
The approved route stops at a reviewable handoff bundle rather than treating a prototype as production-ready software.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Design is a beta Anthropic design surface for visual drafts and prototypes whose actual access depends on plan, organization settings, supported client, rollout, and shared usage limits.
anchors.surfacePath: Claude Design product page > Get started guide > account-specific availability check
anchors.inspectionContext: Public web surfaces observed from macOS 26.5.2; no learner account or organization setting was inspected
availabilityAssumptions: The learner has a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise subscription on which Claude Design is available.
Enterprise access may require an administrator to enable Claude Design.
The learner uses a supported web or desktop surface and has remaining shared Claude usage.
expectedEvidence: Current first-party pages identify Claude Design as beta and list Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans.
The Help Center limits the surface to web and desktop and documents shared usage and known limitations.
Public page reachability is not treated as proof of account-specific access.
changeTriggers: Claude Design beta status, plan availability, client support, or usage policy changes
Enterprise enablement or rollout behavior changes

conflicts.summary: The launch announcement says research preview while the current product and Help Center pages say beta.
conflicts.disposition: Teach beta as the current status and retain the launch wording only as historical evidence; recheck account availability at use time.

recertificationEvidence.surfacePath: Claude Design product page > Get started guide > account-specific availability check
observations: The current product and Help Center surfaces identify Claude Design as beta and list supported paid plans.
The Help Center records web and desktop availability, shared usage, and known collaboration, comment, large-repository, and import limitations.
No account-specific access claim was made because no learner account or organization settings were inspected.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Design creates editable visual drafts and interactive prototypes for exploration, feedback, and user testing, but neither generation nor shareability proves product correctness or production readiness.
anchors.inspectionContext: Public product and launch contracts inspected from macOS 26.5.2; no generated prototype was treated as verified evidence
anchors.principleStatement: Use the prototype to compare directions and collect observable feedback from real tasks; preserve the distinction between a testable design artifact and implemented, reviewed, production-ready software.
changeTriggers: Claude Design prototype or handoff positioning changes
The product begins making a materially different production-readiness claim

observations: The product page positions interactive prototypes as artifacts to test with real people and separates them from code review.
The launch announcement describes prototypes, product mockups, exploration, sharing, and handoff; it does not certify production correctness.

anchors.claimScope: A bounded Claude Design brief declares goal, layout, content, audience, and relevant product context so both generation and review have explicit criteria.
anchors.inspectionContext: Current Help Center prompt contract inspected from macOS 26.5.2
anchors.principleStatement: Write the brief before generating: name the user and goal, layout, real content, intended devices, design-system context, accessibility expectations, and acceptance evidence.
changeTriggers: Claude Design prompt or context guidance changes

observations: The current guide requires a goal, layout, content, and audience and recommends attaching screenshots, assets, codebases, or design files as context.
The anchor adds acceptance evidence as the course boundary, not as a claim that the product guide validates the result.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Design distinguishes organization design-system setup, review, test, and publication from project-level import or synchronization; output quality remains bounded by source quality and human validation.
anchors.inspectionContext: Current Help Center setup and project-import contracts inspected from macOS 26.5.2
anchors.principleStatement: Record the source, generated tokens and components, test-project comparison, and Published state for organization setup; record imported source and sample fidelity for project sync, without treating either operation as proof of brand fidelity.
changeTriggers: Organization setup, Published state, import sources, or design-sync behavior changes

observations: The setup guide requires review of generated tokens and components, a test project, and an explicit Published toggle.
The project guide supports GitHub, design-file, upload, and local-codebase imports and warns that import quality follows source quality.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Design supports comparing alternative directions and preserving a prior project state before exploring a materially different approach; the learner must record the selection criteria and revision identity.
anchors.inspectionContext: Current Help Center refinement and revision guidance inspected from macOS 26.5.2
anchors.principleStatement: Define criteria before generation, compare genuinely different alternatives, name the selected revision and trade-off, and preserve a recoverable prior state before exploring another direction.
changeTriggers: Claude Design alternatives, comments, direct-edit, or revision behavior changes

observations: The guide calls the first generation a starting point, supports 2–3 alternative layouts, and separates chat, comments, and direct canvas editing.
Its revision guidance preserves the current project before trying a different direction; the course selection rationale remains learner-authored evidence.

anchors.claimScope: Responsive and interaction claims about a Claude Design prototype require direct observation across declared viewport sizes, states, inputs, and task paths; prompt text or generated interactivity alone is not verification.
anchors.inspectionContext: Public product guidance inspected from macOS 26.5.2; no prototype output was certified without direct learner observation
anchors.principleStatement: Declare device targets and state transitions in the brief, then resize and operate the prototype through the core task with relevant pointer, keyboard, error, loading, and empty states; record observations and deviations.
changeTriggers: Claude Design responsive prompting, prototype interaction, or preview behavior changes

observations: The Help Center tells authors to identify mobile, tablet, and desktop requirements early.
The product page presents prototypes as interactive artifacts for real-person testing, so the anchor requires observation rather than inferring behavior from generation.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Design can suggest accessibility, contrast, hierarchy, and usability improvements, but accessibility evidence requires testable criteria and a combination of automated checks and human evaluation.
anchors.inspectionContext: Current Anthropic guidance and W3C Recommendation inspected from macOS 26.5.2; no conformance audit was performed
anchors.principleStatement: Treat Claude feedback as a candidate checklist, choose applicable WCAG 2.2 criteria, and collect keyboard, focus, reflow, contrast, semantics, error, and user evidence; do not convert an AI review into a conformance claim.
changeTriggers: Claude Design accessibility-review behavior changes
The selected W3C Recommendation or evaluation guidance changes

observations: Anthropic describes Claude as a design collaborator that can review accessibility, not as an auditor or conformance authority.
WCAG 2.2 supplies testable success criteria, and W3C evaluation guidance requires more than a single automated or model-generated check.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Design can hand a selected design to Claude Code or connected tools, but the handoff must preserve design intent and evidence and does not authorize repository writes or prove implementation fidelity.
anchors.inspectionContext: Current Help Center and launch handoff contracts inspected from macOS 26.5.2; no account connection or repository write was performed
anchors.principleStatement: Bundle source and revision, intent, states, responsive and accessibility rules, prototype observations, scope, and unresolved assumptions; reconnect or import only through the current documented surface and grant repository authority separately.
changeTriggers: Claude Design export, MCP, design-sync, design-login, or Claude Code handoff behavior changes

observations: The guide documents design-sync, Claude Design MCP, design-login, export, and Claude Code handoff surfaces.
The launch announcement says the handoff packages design work for Claude Code; neither source grants repository authority or verifies the resulting implementation.

anchors.claimScope: Phase 6 is a repository-delivery route that begins after Code readiness and ends only with an implemented, deterministically checked, reviewed closeout tied to the delivered checkpoint.
anchors.principleStatement: Enter Engineering only after Code readiness, select the fitting on-ramp, preserve deterministic evidence, and stop only after Review evidence matches the final checkpoint.
changeTriggers: The approved Engineering route, readiness requirement, or closeout contract changes

observations: Issue #13 defines Engineering as an end-to-end repository delivery route rather than a collection of isolated skill demos.
The approved route requires Code readiness before entry and an immutable, reviewed closeout before completion.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Code can map an unfamiliar repository by starting at the project root, requesting a high-level overview, narrowing to relevant files, and tracing execution flow before any implementation edit.
anchors.inspectionContext: Claude Code documentation surface checked from macOS 26.5.2, arm64; contract inspection only
anchors.principleStatement: Map before editing: establish the repository root, structure, conventions, domain terms, relevant files, interactions, and execution flow using read-only investigation, then carry the map into request alignment.
changeTriggers: Anthropic changes its codebase exploration workflow
The course read-only reconnaissance or Engineering entry boundary changes

observations: The first-party workflow starts at the project root, requests a codebase overview, then narrows into architecture, data models, conventions, and project terminology.
The same workflow separately traces relevant files, their interactions, and execution flow; Issue #13 keeps this investigation read-only before repository delivery.

anchors.claimScope: The current Ask Matt router distinguishes the idea-to-ship flow, triage and diagnosis on-ramps, architecture upkeep, Wayfinder planning, and session handoff without collapsing their evidence boundaries.
anchors.inspectionContext: macOS 26.5.2, arm64, zsh; immutable Git checkout and contract inspection
anchors.principleStatement: Choose the engineering flow by work shape and preserve the handoff between planning, delivery, review, diagnosis, architecture, and Wayfinder instead of invoking every skill as one linear checklist.
changeTriggers: The upstream Ask Matt route changes
The pinned upstream revision is superseded for course use

conflicts.summary: The legacy Phase 3 repo-map lesson names a skill that is absent from the current upstream engineering skill set.
conflicts.disposition: Do not claim a current repo-map skill; anchor the canonical repository-map lesson to the first-party Claude Code reconnaissance contract instead.

observations: The pinned Ask Matt contract separates the main idea-to-ship flow from triage, diagnosis, architecture, and Wayfinder on-ramps.
The legacy repo-map skill is no longer present upstream, so the canonical course does not teach it as an available skill.

anchors.claimScope: Engineering request shaping uses repository-aware grilling for decisions and a throwaway prototype only when a runnable answer is needed before the delivery spec.
anchors.inspectionContext: macOS 26.5.2, arm64, zsh; immutable Git checkout and contract inspection
anchors.principleStatement: Resolve conversational uncertainty with repository-aware grilling; detour through a deliberately throwaway prototype only for a concrete technical question, then carry the decision back into the delivery flow.
changeTriggers: Upstream grilling or prototype boundaries change
Prototype output becomes a production deliverable in the approved route

observations: The pinned grilling contract preserves repository decisions in project documentation.
The pinned prototype contract treats code as disposable evidence for one design question, not the implementation candidate.

anchors.claimScope: The current delivery flow turns settled decisions into a spec, slices tracer-bullet tickets with blocking edges, implements each ticket test-first, reviews the fixed candidate, and hands context across sessions when needed.
anchors.inspectionContext: macOS 26.5.2, arm64, zsh; immutable Git checkout and contract inspection
anchors.principleStatement: Preserve the sequence from settled decisions to spec, dependency-aware tickets, test-first implementation, fixed-point review, commit, and session handoff; each artifact carries evidence into the next step without replacing it.
changeTriggers: Upstream spec, ticket, implement, TDD, or handoff contracts change
The course changes its issue dependency or review checkpoint model

observations: The pinned contracts preserve one flow from spec through dependency-aware tickets to TDD implementation and review.
Handoff is explicitly a context bridge and does not substitute for deterministic checks or final Review evidence.

anchors.claimScope: Repository review compares an immutable candidate against a fixed point on two independent axes: documented standards and the originating spec.
anchors.inspectionContext: macOS 26.5.2, arm64, zsh; immutable Git checkout and contract inspection
anchors.principleStatement: Pin the candidate and fixed point, review Standards and Spec independently, and invalidate all review evidence when the candidate changes.
changeTriggers: The upstream two-axis Review contract changes
The project immutable checkpoint rule changes

observations: The pinned Review contract keeps Standards and Spec findings separate and compares the diff to a fixed point.
Issue #13 requires the reviewed candidate to be immutable and requires a full rerun after mutation.

anchors.claimScope: Triage is reserved for externally arriving issues or pull requests and moves each item through explicit category and state roles before implementation.
anchors.inspectionContext: macOS 26.5.2, arm64, zsh; immutable Git checkout and contract inspection
anchors.principleStatement: Use triage for raw external requests, verify the claim and repository context, then assign exactly one category role and one state role; generated delivery tickets are already agent-ready and bypass triage.
changeTriggers: The upstream triage state machine or issue-versus-PR boundary changes

observations: The pinned contract limits triage to external reports and requests, including configured external PRs.
It requires claim verification and separates category roles from workflow state roles before handoff to implementation.

anchors.claimScope: Hard-bug diagnosis must establish a tight deterministic feedback loop before theorizing, then preserve the fix with a regression test and capture architectural follow-through separately.
anchors.inspectionContext: macOS 26.5.2, arm64, zsh; immutable Git checkout and contract inspection
anchors.principleStatement: Do not diagnose from a story alone: create one command that reliably fails for the reported bug, localize the cause with evidence, fix it with a regression test, and route architectural debt to a separate follow-through.
changeTriggers: The upstream diagnosis loop or regression-test boundary changes

observations: The pinned diagnosis contract refuses hypothesis-driven changes until a tight red feedback loop exists.
It preserves the fix with regression evidence and hands architecture concerns to a separate workflow.

anchors.claimScope: Architecture work first surveys for a narrow deepening opportunity, then designs a deep module at a clean seam with explicit domain vocabulary and testable interface evidence.
anchors.inspectionContext: macOS 26.5.2, arm64, zsh; immutable Git checkout and contract inspection
anchors.principleStatement: Separate surveying from designing: identify one evidence-backed deepening opportunity, place a small interface at a clean seam, preserve domain language, and carry the chosen change into the normal delivery flow.
changeTriggers: Upstream architecture survey, deep-module, or domain-modeling vocabulary changes

observations: The pinned architecture survey generates one bounded candidate instead of directly implementing broad cleanup.
The supporting contracts define a deep module, clean seam, testable interface, and durable domain language for the selected candidate.

anchors.claimScope: Wayfinder is a planning flow for efforts larger than one context window: it charts named decision tickets, resolves only the frontier, records decisions on the shared map, and hands the cleared route to specification rather than implementation.
anchors.inspectionContext: macOS 26.5.2, arm64, zsh; immutable Git checkout and contract inspection
anchors.principleStatement: Use Wayfinder only when the route to a large destination is still foggy; chart decisions, work one unblocked frontier ticket per session, maintain the map as an index, then hand a cleared route to specification before implementation.
changeTriggers: The upstream map, frontier, ticket-type, or handoff contract changes

observations: The pinned contract defines the map as an index of named decision tickets and the frontier as open, unblocked, unclaimed work.
It produces decisions rather than deliverables and hands a cleared map to specification instead of skipping directly to implementation.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Code exposes version and help commands, and starts an interactive session when invoked without print mode.
availabilityAssumptions: Claude Code is installed locally and authentication is handled separately from this non-mutating check.
expectedEvidence: The version command returns 2.1.211 (Claude Code).
The help output identifies the default interactive session and the -p/--print non-interactive mode.
changeTriggers: Claude Code version changes
CLI invocation or authentication guidance changes

observations: claude --version returned 2.1.211 (Claude Code).
claude --help returned the documented interactive and print-mode command surface without starting a session.
The current first-party CLI reference documents the same interactive and -p/--print entry points.

anchors.claimScope: The canonical production host serves the frozen pre-migration index identity and has not partially published the route-based catalog.
availabilityAssumptions: The Vercel Production alias remains the canonical public host.
Remote main remains pinned to the frozen pre-migration commit until coherent cutover.
expectedEvidence: The production index returns HTTP 200 and matches the frozen Git blob byte-for-byte.
All 73 frozen baseline URLs remain resolvable and no remote migration branch exists.
changeTriggers: The production deployment SHA changes
The canonical host or deployment trigger changes
A remote migration branch or Preview deployment appears

observations: On 2026-07-16 the online Freeze verifier observed the production baseline at the frozen pre-migration identity and the index bytes matched SHA-256 cae763f33a866da38b0ff4d8b7a06907a4715a38c6f6cd76432470d40f0a9de5.
The same live observation returned ONLINE URLS PASS (73/73) and confirmed the local-only migration branch had not produced a partial publication.

anchors.claimScope: Repository delivery review must target an immutable candidate, and any candidate change requires a new checkpoint and full review contract rerun.
anchors.principleStatement: Review evidence is valid only for the exact immutable final candidate; a changed candidate receives a new checkpoint and a complete rerun.
changeTriggers: The approved migration Review contract changes
The project adopts a different immutable candidate identity model

observations: Issue #13 explicitly binds repository delivery to an immutable Review checkpoint.
Issue #13 explicitly requires a new checkpoint and full Review contract rerun after any candidate mutation.

anchors.claimScope: Claude, Cowork, Claude Code, and Claude Design are distinct first-party work surfaces whose documented output and interaction boundaries determine the shared product-selection entry point across routes.
anchors.surfacePath: Claude product overview > Cowork product page > Claude Design product page > Claude Code overview
availabilityAssumptions: Public Anthropic product pages are reachable.
Actual product availability may vary by plan, account, region, and rollout state.
expectedEvidence: The overview presents Claude as the general problem-solving surface and links to specialized products.
Cowork is described for delegated cross-file and connected-app knowledge work.
Claude Design is described for visual drafts such as prototypes, decks, and one-pagers.
Claude Code is documented as an agentic coding tool that works in a codebase and development environment.
changeTriggers: Anthropic changes a product name or surface boundary
A required surface changes plan or platform availability
The product overview removes or replaces one of the selected surfaces

recertificationEvidence.surfacePath: Claude product overview > Cowork product page > Claude Design product page > Claude Code overview
observations: All four first-party pages returned current product content on 2026-07-16.
The pages keep the surfaces distinct by task shape: general problem solving, knowledge work, visual design, and codebase delivery.
The shared product picker owns this cross-route selection claim; route-specific Design prototype anchors are not duplicated in its page mapping.
Availability is explicitly treated as an assumption rather than inferred from page reachability.

anchors.claimScope: Cowork can carry a bounded knowledge-work task across files and connected tools to a reviewable deliverable, while the learner remains responsible for scope and review.
anchors.surfacePath: Claude Cowork product page > product guide > first bounded task
availabilityAssumptions: The learner has a Claude plan and platform on which Cowork is available.
The starter task uses copied or otherwise recoverable files and no sensitive production data.
Connected apps are optional for the starter and require separate authorization.
expectedEvidence: The product page describes goal-directed work across files and tools with a polished result returned for review.
The product guide distinguishes Cowork knowledge work from Claude Code coding work and keeps human review in the workflow.
changeTriggers: Cowork task or file-access behavior changes
Cowork platform or plan availability changes
The first-party starter guidance changes its review or safety boundary

recertificationEvidence.surfacePath: Claude Cowork product page > product guide > first bounded task
observations: The product page states that Cowork works across files and tools and returns work for review.
The official product guide describes Cowork as a knowledge-work agent and identifies Claude Code as the coding surface.
No claim was made that the product page proves account-specific availability or connected-app authorization.

anchors.claimScope: Phase 1 produces readiness evidence only: safe scope, route choice, bounded fixture practice, learner judgment, and a clear distinction between practice and repository delivery.
anchors.principleStatement: Orient ends with evidence that the learner can choose a route and work safely in a readiness fixture; it does not produce a real repository deliverable or route completion.
changeTriggers: The approved Phase 1 boundary changes
Readiness evidence or course completion definitions change

observations: Issue #13 defines Phase 1 as an onboarding and readiness hub whose outcome is route choice and readiness evidence.
Issue #13 states that Cowork starter is an onboarding branch and readiness-fixture practice is not a real repository deliverable.
Issue #13 requires safe scope, verifiable success, read-only reconnaissance, plan, bounded edit, checks, and controlled commit evidence.

anchors.claimScope: The installed Claude Code CLI exposes bounded execution controls for permissions, model and effort, agents, MCP configuration, worktree isolation, allowed tools, and non-interactive print mode.
availabilityAssumptions: Claude Code 2.1.211 is installed as the native binary.
The check inspects local help and does not authenticate, start a session, or invoke a model.
expectedEvidence: The binary resolves to Claude Code 2.1.211.
Help lists --permission-mode, --model, --effort, --agent, --worktree, --allowedTools, --mcp-config, and -p/--print.
MCP help lists non-mutating discovery commands and explicit add/remove configuration commands.
changeTriggers: Claude Code version changes
A required CLI flag or command changes
The documented safety or execution boundary for a flag changes

observations: The installed binary hash remained 5a728a76198b6eca7f3c7cdbff43bab44b77b48c2108f7a3107d889773382629.
Local help exposed every required bounded execution flag without starting a session.
Local MCP help identified project approval state and separated read-only list/get from configuration mutations.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Code permissions are enforced by the application, deny rules take precedence, and plan mode permits exploration while preventing source edits.
anchors.principleStatement: Use application-enforced permission rules and plan mode to bound tool authority; prompts and CLAUDE.md influence intent but do not grant permissions.
changeTriggers: Permission precedence or plan-mode behavior changes
A required permission mode is renamed or removed
Managed permission policy semantics change

observations: The permissions reference states that read-only file and search tools do not require approval within allowed directories.
The reference defines deny, ask, then allow precedence and states that enforcement belongs to Claude Code rather than the model.
The current permission-mode table defines plan as read-only exploration without source edits, and the CLI reference exposes --permission-mode.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Code model selection controls capability while effort controls how much work the agent attempts; availability and accepted effort levels remain model, account, provider, and version dependent.
anchors.principleStatement: Choose model for the capability needed and effort for the desired thoroughness; verify available choices in the current surface instead of teaching moving aliases or every documented level as universal.
changeTriggers: Claude model aliases or defaults change
Effort levels or persistence semantics change
Plan, provider, or organization availability changes

conflicts.summary: The current CLI reference documents ultracode for v2.1.203+, while local Claude Code 2.1.211 help lists low, medium, high, xhigh, and max only.
conflicts.disposition: Exclude ultracode from the shared required claim and teach only choices observed in the learner's current surface; a future ultracode lesson requires separate reproduction.

observations: The first-party guide distinguishes fixed model capability from effort-driven breadth, tool use, and verification.
The model configuration reference says availability depends on account, provider, and organizational settings.
The local help discrepancy for ultracode was bounded as an optional-path conflict rather than hidden or generalized.
The shared model and effort reference owns selection guidance; route lessons consume the same anchor rather than defining competing aliases or defaults.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Code hooks are deterministic lifecycle callbacks whose event, matcher, command, input, output, and blocking semantics must be smoke-tested before use as guardrails.
anchors.principleStatement: A hook claim is valid only when its exact lifecycle event and matcher run in a recoverable fixture and its allow or block result is observed; configuration presence alone is not evidence.
changeTriggers: Hook event or matcher semantics change
Blocking exit-code or JSON output behavior changes
Hook configuration locations or input schema change

observations: The hooks guide defines lifecycle events and matcher-scoped commands and states that the /hooks browser is read-only.
The guardrail example uses PreToolUse with an Edit|Write matcher and exit code 2 to block protected-file edits.
The anchor deliberately certifies the hook contract, not an unexecuted lesson-specific hook result.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Code skills are directory-scoped instruction packages rooted at SKILL.md that can be discovered automatically or invoked explicitly, so Equip should use an existing skill before authoring a new shared workflow.
anchors.principleStatement: Equip may select and smoke-test an existing skill; creating a reusable shared skill is a Standardize responsibility and must not be smuggled into the toolbox lesson.
changeTriggers: Skill discovery, invocation, or scope changes
SKILL.md packaging requirements change
The approved Equip versus Standardize boundary changes

observations: The official skill reference requires SKILL.md and distinguishes personal, project, and plugin locations.
The reference states that skills may load when relevant or be invoked by name.
Issue #13 keeps Phase 2 to using existing capabilities and moves shared workflow authoring to Phase 9.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Code MCP connections expose external tools and data, require explicit trust and scope choices, and should begin with the minimum read-only capability needed by the active route.
anchors.principleStatement: Connect only a trusted MCP server, choose the narrowest local, project, or user scope, approve project configuration explicitly, and expose only the read capability required for the exercise.
changeTriggers: MCP transport, trust, approval, or scope semantics change
The Anthropic Directory or prompt-injection guidance changes
The course minimum-authority boundary changes

observations: The MCP reference warns learners to verify trust because fetched external content can carry prompt-injection risk.
The reference distinguishes local, project, and user installation scopes and keeps unapproved project servers pending.
Issue #13 requires a trusted source and minimum read-only permission for the Phase 2 MCP lesson.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Code can isolate bounded investigation in read-only subagents and isolate parallel file edits in separate git worktrees; these solve different context and filesystem collision risks.
anchors.principleStatement: Use a fresh read-only Explore or Plan subagent for bounded investigation; use a worktree when parallel sessions may edit files, because context isolation alone does not isolate the filesystem.
changeTriggers: Built-in subagent tool boundaries change
Worktree creation, branch, location, or cleanup behavior changes
Desktop and CLI worktree behavior diverges

observations: The subagent reference defines Explore and Plan as read-only and denies Write and Edit.
The worktree reference states that worktrees isolate edits and documents --worktree under .claude/worktrees/.
The worktree reference explicitly distinguishes edit isolation from subagent coordination.

anchors.claimScope: Claude Code non-interactive execution uses -p/--print and explicit tool, output, budget, and configuration flags; CI adds repository permissions, secret handling, and untrusted-input boundaries that must remain explicit.
anchors.principleStatement: A headless or CI exercise must declare prompt, allowed tools, output form, budget, credentials, repository permissions, and stop conditions; local one-shot evidence does not prove remote CI authorization.
changeTriggers: Non-interactive flags or context-loading behavior changes
Claude Code GitHub Actions setup, permissions, or secret guidance changes
The action major version or security contract changes

observations: The headless reference requires -p/--print and documents allowed tools, structured output, budget, and explicit configuration.
The reference warns that normal non-interactive mode loads project and user context unless bare mode is deliberately selected.
The GitHub Actions reference separately documents app permissions, repository secrets, and allowed/disallowed tool controls.

anchors.claimScope: Phase 2 is a just-in-time toolbox selected by the active route; it has no phase completion state and returns the learner after one bounded capability smoke test.
anchors.principleStatement: Choose only the capability required by the active route, record permissions, side effects, stop and return points, run one safe smoke test, then return; Equip is not a feature tour or completion ladder.
changeTriggers: The approved Phase 2 boundary or toolbox route changes
Equip gains a completion state or workflow-authoring responsibility

observations: Issue #13 defines Phase 2 as a task-selected toolbox with no overall completion state.
Issue #13 requires permission, side-effect, stop-condition, return-point, and safe-smoke-test evidence.
Issue #13 keeps shared workflow authoring in Phase 9 and requires return to the active route.

anchors.claimScope: The core Knowledge Work route turns attributable source material into one learner-reviewed knowledge artifact and stops only when deliverable, provenance, verification, judgment, and feedback evidence are reviewable together.
anchors.principleStatement: Select one mission-fitting artifact branch, preserve its sources, produce and verify a bounded slice, record learner judgment and feedback, then stop at Knowledge delivery closeout; optional formats and local tools are not a required ladder.
changeTriggers: The approved Knowledge Work route, artifact-branch boundary, or closeout evidence changes

observations: Issue #13 defines Knowledge Work as a task route that produces one reviewable report, document, data artifact, or local knowledge-base slice.
Issue #13 requires raw-source provenance, learner judgment, feedback, and a legal stop at Knowledge delivery closeout.
LLM Wiki and local ingest, search, or analysis tools remain conditional branches rather than core-route completion requirements.

anchors.claimScope: Core Knowledge Work keeps raw sources distinct from generated output, preserves source identity and rights boundaries, traces retained claims to evidence, and records unsupported, conflicting, or uncertain claims before delivery.
anchors.principleStatement: Treat raw sources as the source of truth, assign stable local source IDs, connect every material claim to supporting evidence, label uncertainty and conflict, and verify rights, limitations, target format, and feedback before closeout.
changeTriggers: The approved raw-source, provenance, source-to-claim, rights, or limitation evidence contract changes

observations: Issue #13 requires preserving raw sources and provenance so generated content never becomes the source of truth.
Issue #13 requires a source-to-claim outline and explicit verification of claims, rights, limitations, and target format.
The route closeout combines the deliverable with provenance references, learner judgment, and feedback evidence.

anchors.claimScope: LLM Wiki is an optional local-knowledge-base artifact branch that compiles a bounded, attributable source set into reviewable linked pages and machine-readable exports without replacing raw sources or shared Knowledge verification.
anchors.principleStatement: Select LLM Wiki only when the mission needs a maintained local knowledge-base slice; preserve raw sources and stable IDs, inspect a small generated topic cluster and its links, record omissions and unsupported claims, then return to the common Knowledge verification path.
changeTriggers: LLM Wiki input, generated artifact, export, review, or local-data behavior changes

observations: The project documents local searchable and interlinked wiki output plus AI-consumable exports from supported agent sessions.
Issue #29 keeps LLM Wiki conditional and requires its branch to return to the Knowledge route.

anchors.claimScope: MarkItDown is a lightweight optional conversion surface for turning supported local files into structure-preserving Markdown for text analysis, with process-level I/O authority and no claim of human-layout fidelity.
anchors.principleStatement: Use MarkItDown only when a supported source needs lightweight Markdown normalization; bound file access, retain the raw file, compare headings, tables and omissions against the original, and treat conversion output as a derived working copy.
changeTriggers: MarkItDown supported formats, CLI, security guidance, or conversion behavior changes

observations: The first-party README describes Markdown output for supported document formats and says the output targets text analysis rather than high-fidelity human conversion.
The security guidance says conversion has the current process I/O privileges and recommends narrow input handling.

anchors.claimScope: Docling is an optional local document-conversion surface for supported structured or layout-heavy sources, with explicit output formats and remote services disabled unless deliberately enabled.
anchors.principleStatement: Choose Docling when layout, tables, OCR, or structured conversion needs inspection beyond a lightweight pass; constrain accepted inputs and outputs, keep remote services and external plugins off unless authorized, compare a sampled conversion with the raw source, and preserve limitations.
changeTriggers: Docling CLI, supported inputs, output formats, model behavior, remote-service defaults, or plugin controls change

anchors.claimScope: A durable browser claim is a minimal Playwright Test whose user-observable assertion fails against a controlled faulty fixture and passes under the same test identity after the fixture is corrected; the run records an exact environment, and trace is retained only when failure diagnosis needs it.

declaredEnvironment.browser: system Google Chrome through Playwright chromium launcher

availabilityAssumptions: The learner has Code readiness, permission to add or run a repository test, and a safe controlled fixture rather than a production mutation.
The repository's own instructions and pinned Playwright setup take precedence over the isolated recertification setup.
A compatible browser binary and permission to create then clean test artifacts are available.
steps: Create an isolated /tmp/t26-playwright project pinned to @playwright/test@1.61.1 with one test named guest can complete the controlled checkout fixture.
Use one controlled HTML fixture whose FAULTY_FIXTURE mode changes the post-click heading from 訂單完成 to 仍在處理 without changing the test identity.
Run FAULTY_FIXTURE=1 TRACE_MODE=0 /tmp/t26-playwright/node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config=/tmp/t26-playwright/playwright.config.mjs and require the exact heading assertion to fail.
Run FAULTY_FIXTURE=0 TRACE_MODE=0 /tmp/t26-playwright/node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config=/tmp/t26-playwright/playwright.config.mjs and require the same named test to pass.
Only for unresolved diagnosis, run FAULTY_FIXTURE=1 TRACE_MODE=1 with trace=retain-on-failure and require a non-empty trace.zip artifact.
Run the corrected fixture again with TRACE_MODE=0 and confirm the normal bypass path produces no trace.zip.
expectedEvidence: The controlled faulty fixture fails because the exact heading 訂單完成 is absent, demonstrating that the assertion can disagree with broken behavior.
The corrected fixture passes under the identical test name and assertion in the same declared environment.
The diagnostic run retains trace.zip only when TRACE_MODE=1 and a failure occurs; the ordinary green rerun with trace off produces no trace artifact.
changeTriggers: Playwright Test assertion, retry, trace configuration, package version, browser launch, or artifact behavior changes
The approved Browser Evidence durable-test, declared-environment, trace, or addendum boundary changes

environment.browser: system Google Chrome through Playwright chromium launcher

steps: Created the isolated pinned package, controlled HTML fixture, one Playwright Test, and conditional trace configuration in /tmp/t26-playwright.

FAULTY_FIXTURE=0 TRACE_MODE=0 /tmp/t26-playwright/node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config=/tmp/t26-playwright/playwright.config.mjs --output=/tmp/t26-bypass-output and verified no trace.zip existed
observations: The faulty mode failed the exact getByRole heading assertion with element(s) not found; this was an intended behavior failure rather than setup failure.
The corrected mode passed the same guest can complete the controlled checkout fixture test without changing its assertion or identity.
The diagnostic failure produced a non-empty trace.zip under retain-on-failure, while the corrected TRACE_MODE=0 rerun passed and produced no trace artifact.
Retries remained zero so the deliberate RED was not hidden or relabeled as flaky.
